# Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization

## Archive
path: inbox/2026/10/ad929b9ee3.html

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces Turbo Harness, a framework for instance-adaptive harness optimization.
- Recycles artifacts from global harness optimization into a structured playbook.
- Trains a harness editor to generate instance-specific patches to the global harness.
- Enables tailored harness construction at inference time for each task instance.
- Demonstrates consistent outperformance over existing baselines across seven diverse benchmarks.

### Method
Turbo Harness leverages information from a completed global harness optimization run by summarizing artifacts into a playbook and training a harness editor that uses this playbook along with instance data to create customized harness patches, enabling instance-specific execution models.

### Result
Turbo Harness consistently outperforms existing harness optimization baselines on seven benchmarks spanning interactive agent tasks, software engineering, and long-horizon terminal tasks, showing improved instance-level harness effectiveness.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to agent harnesses and context management, agent self-improvement, reasoning-time planning, and agent evaluation; advances instance-adaptive optimization critical for autonomous agents and agentic frameworks.

# EVOHARNESSBENCH: Can Your Agents Keep Pace with an Evolving Harness?

## Archive
path: inbox/2026/09/b2cf687fa6.html

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces EVOHARNESSBENCH, a benchmark for evaluating LLM-based agents under evolving harness conditions across tools, skills, and agents.
- Defines 17 multi-stage harness streams with 802 tasks, 520 tools, 42 skills, and 62 agents for controlled evaluation.
- Identifies harness-induced forgetting where expanding harness degrades performance on previously solved tasks.
- Evaluates deployment and self-evolving adaptation settings to test retention and adaptation capabilities.
- Reveals retention of earlier competence and adaptation to new capabilities can conflict, highlighting challenges in agent evolution.

### Method
Constructs deterministic multi-stage harness streams from verifier-based benchmarks to simulate controlled harness evolution; evaluates agents on retention and adaptation through deployment and self-evolving adaptation scenarios.

### Result
Finds persistent challenges including harness-induced forgetting, inconsistent gains from self-evolving adaptation, and tension between retaining old skills and adapting to new ones, establishing harness evolution as a distinct challenge for autonomous agents.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to LLM-based autonomous agents, agent evaluation benchmarks, agent self-improvement, tool use, and multi-agent systems, directly addressing challenges in evolving agentic frameworks and retention-adaptation trade-offs.
note.title: EVOHARNESSBENCH: Can Your Agents Keep Pace with an Evolving Harness?

# Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/09/2609.11677.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Identifies lack of principled failure diagnosis as bottleneck in runtime harness evolution for LLM agents
- Proposes Ecdysis framework to distinguish model-specific issues from harness-level defects
- Introduces batch-level cross-instance failure aggregation to analyze recurring failure patterns
- Develops Failure-Driven Collaborative Refinement for iterative harness modification
- Achieves up to 1.84x speedup in harness training compared to existing methods
- Improves reasoning accuracy of harnesses by 18.56%

### Method
Ecdysis framework combines cross-instance failure analysis with multi-role diagnosis to efficiently and effectively evolve runtime harnesses by focusing on systematic harness deficiencies rather than individual model-specific failures.

### Result
Ecdysis significantly reduces training time for runtime harnesses while enhancing their reasoning accuracy, demonstrating superior performance over traditional iterative search-based harness evolution methods.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to AI-assisted software engineering, particularly in improving agentic coding workflows and autonomous software engineering agents by optimizing runtime harness training for LLM agents, which can enhance AI coding assistants' capabilities and developer experience.
note.title: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents

# Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/09/2609.24974.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces agent harness distillation to transfer optimized harness behaviors into model weights for deployment with a fixed harness
- Proposes Harness-Zero, enabling harness distillation via agent-as-harness correcting student responses before execution
- Demonstrates that agent-as-harness outperforms code-as-harness for frontier LLMs using evolved harnesses
- Shows Harness-Zero improves task success rates beyond using specialized harness at deployment
- Recovers 82.3% of harness-induced behaviors absent from base models across multiple domains

### Method
Harness-Zero uses an optimized harness to guide a harnessing agent that corrects student agent responses in the target harness action space, generating training demonstrations. Fine-tuning on these trajectories internalizes specialized harness behaviors into the model, allowing removal of the specialized harness at deployment.

### Result
Harness-Zero improves macro-average task success from 23.3% to 44.3% without the specialized harness at deployment, exceeding the 41.7% success rate when the harness is still attached, and recovers 82.3% of specialized behaviors across 28 patterns in knowledge work, tool use, and science domains.

### Relevance
HIGH INTEREST: Advances agent harnesses and context management, agent self-improvement, tool use, and agent evaluation in LLM-based autonomous agents and agentic frameworks. Medium relevance to LLM fine-tuning for agent behavior and multi-modal agents. Low relevance to general NLP, robotics, and unrelated AI topics.
note.title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness

# RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/09/2609.24972.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces RRSI, a regularized recursive self-improvement framework for LLM agent harnesses
- Proposes a proposer with temporally annealed budget encouraging exploration of new evolution trajectories
- Implements a selector with a critic and pruner to filter benchmark-specific or inefficient edits
- Demonstrates improved out-of-distribution generalization and efficiency across eight diverse benchmarks
- Achieves up to 14.1 points gain on evolved split and 4.7 points on out-of-distribution tasks
- Reduces policy token usage by 30% compared to unregularized evolution

### Method
RRSI constrains recursive self-improvement of agent harnesses by limiting edit proposals via an annealed budget and encouraging unexplored trajectories, while a selector uses a critic to screen benchmark-specific changes and a pruner to remove small, costly, or obsolete edits, promoting reusable agent mechanisms.

### Result
RRSI improves agent harness performance with up to 14.1 points gain on training splits and up to 4.7 points on out-of-distribution benchmarks, while reducing policy token consumption by 30%, demonstrating better generalization and efficiency.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to LLM-based autonomous agents, agent harness design, self-improvement, context management, tool use, and evaluation benchmarks, aligning well with interests in agentic frameworks, memory architectures, planning, and safety.

# Recursive Video In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.06843.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced Recursive Video In-Context Learning (RV-ICL), a training-free method to hierarchically navigate demonstration videos for robotic tasks
- Developed a hierarchical structure of demonstration sub-events from coarse keyframes to fine short clips for detailed task execution
- Enabled agents to dynamically access relevant video clips during task execution to improve planning and manipulation
- Demonstrated that one demonstration per task suffices for effective learning with RV-ICL
- Achieved improved success rates on LIBERO-PRO and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks compared to prior methods

### Method
RV-ICL builds a hierarchical representation of demonstration videos segmented into sub-events (grasps, releases, etc.) with multiple levels of granularity. The agent reads coarse levels for planning and recursively accesses finer clips as needed during execution, enabling efficient and detailed task understanding without additional training.

### Result
RV-ICL improved success rates from 92.6% to 96.5% on LIBERO-PRO and from 86.7% to 95.8% on LIBERO-Plus benchmarks, demonstrating enhanced robotic manipulation performance with a single demonstration per task.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to humanoid robotics, embodied AI, robot learning from demonstration, vision-language-action models, and dexterous manipulation, aligning with interests in physical AI and robot perception.
note.title: Recursive Video In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot

# Rho: A Foundation for Efficiently Adaptable VLA Models

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/09/2609.38164.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced Rho, a family of open-weight VLA models for bimanual manipulation across multiple robot embodiments
- Demonstrated embodiment midtraining improves downstream task adaptation
- Developed an internal latent policy enabling online adaptation from corrective feedback
- Achieved state-of-the-art performance across tasks and robot embodiments compared to existing open-weight VLAs
- Released base and embodiment-specific Rho model checkpoints for research and industrial use

### Method
Designed an action-expert architecture and training recipe for Rho models, incorporating embodiment midtraining and a latent policy for observation-conditioned noise input selection to enable data-light task adaptation and online learning.

### Result
Rho models matched or outperformed existing open-weight VLA models on three dual-arm robot embodiments in simulation and physical experiments, showing strong general-purpose robotic manipulation capabilities and practical adaptability with as few as 15 corrected episodes.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to humanoid robotics, embodied AI, robot learning for manipulation, vision-language-action models, sim-to-real transfer, and foundation models applied to robotics, aligning with high-interest topics in physical AI and dexterous manipulation.

# FlowWAM: Optical Flow as a Unified Action Representation for World Action Models

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/07/2607.13017.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced FlowWAM, a dual-stream diffusion framework using optical flow as a unified action representation for world action models.
- Demonstrated that flow-based action representation aligns with pretrained video generators and encodes rich per-pixel motion cues.
- Enabled leveraging large-scale action-unlabeled video datasets for pretraining due to flow extraction from raw videos.
- Achieved state-of-the-art success rates on RoboTwin manipulation tasks, outperforming VLA and WAM baselines.
- Improved trajectory accuracy significantly on WorldArena world modeling with an 18.4% relative gain in EWMScore.

### Method
FlowWAM employs optical flow videos as a unified, video-native action representation within a shared pretrained video generator, supporting both policy mode for action prediction and world-model mode for guiding future video generation.

### Result
FlowWAM raised RoboTwin manipulation success rates to over 92% in both Clean and Random settings and achieved the best overall EWMScore (63.71) on WorldArena world modeling, marking significant improvements over prior baselines.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to humanoid robotics, embodied AI, robot learning for manipulation, vision-language-action models, robot perception, sim-to-real transfer, and dexterous manipulation, aligning with the target profile's high-interest areas.

# LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.22372.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for evaluating preference learning in robotic manipulation separately from task completion.
- Defines a controlled taxonomy of language-expressible preferences covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices.
- Provides five task suites totaling 312 tasks, paired demonstrations, metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics.
- Evaluates zero-shot preference following, learning efficiency, generalization, preference composition, and conflict handling.

### Method
Builds on LIBERO with a procedural pipeline that generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences; evaluates vision-language-action policies and supervised fine-tuning across five task suites.

### Result
Current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while supervised fine-tuning enables preference learning. Mixed training better preserves performance without preferences than sequential adaptation and benefits from contextual prompts, but can weaken motion-preference learning. Generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain challenging.

### Relevance
Strong relevance to embodied AI, robot learning from demonstration, manipulation, and VLA models. It benchmarks how robots adapt behavior to user preferences, a capability important for practical and personalized human-robot interaction.

# Facet-0: A Robotic Foundation Model for Contact-Rich Precise Manipulation

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/09/2609.01596.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced Facet-0, a robotic foundation model predicting and valuing contact consequences for precise manipulation
- Unified multimodal representation learning and reinforcement learning via joint action-wrench proposals
- Developed a distributional Action-Wrench Critic to differentiate motions with similar progress but different contact outcomes
- Implemented phase-aware rewards and contact-selective credit to focus policy improvement on decisive interactions
- Created a lightweight bounded actor for on-robot adaptation using frozen representations
- Trained on a large force-synchronized dataset achieving high success and sub-millimeter accuracy in assembly tasks

### Method
Facet-0 integrates vision-language semantics, kinematic state, and causal wrench history using flow matching to generate action chunks and expected wrist-wrench profiles. Deployment rollouts train an Action-Wrench Critic with phase-aware rewards and contact-selective credit. A bounded actor enables on-robot adaptation while preserving predictive action-contact coupling. The system is trained on a 1,000-hour force-synchronized corpus across multiple embodiments and manufacturing cells.

### Result
Achieved 82% mean success on five sub-millimeter computer-assembly tasks with 0.5 mm placement accuracy and 50 ms command latency, outperforming the strongest baseline at 15% success.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to embodied AI, robot learning for manipulation, vision-language-action models, robot perception, sim-to-real transfer, foundation models in robotics, and dexterous manipulation, aligning with high interest areas in humanoid robotics and physical world understanding.

# RouterVLA: Turning Smoke Tests into Supervision for Heterogeneous VLA Selection

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/06/2606.27355.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces RouterVLA, a method turning smoke tests into supervision for heterogeneous VLA policy selection
- Proposes outcome-disjoint cross-fitting to build profiles for frozen experts and score selected experts separately
- Demonstrates a transparent probe-success rule that improves held-out success rate by +14.64 percentage points
- Shows learned scorers perform similarly to the probe-success rule under scalar-only profiles
- Highlights the importance of outcome separation to avoid inflated gain measurements
- Finds that commissioning-aware routing improves system performance beyond individual policy scaling

### Method
RouterVLA uses outcome-disjoint cross-fitting on pre-deployment rollout records to build expert profiles and select policies based on probe-success rules or learned scorers, ensuring credible evaluation by separating scored trials from profiling data.

### Result
Applying RouterVLA on 34,752 LIBERO-Plus rollout records raised held-out success from 0.4686 to 0.6149 (+14.64pp), with learned scorers matching probe-success rule performance and demonstrating the value of commissioning-aware routing over scalar scorer capacity.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to vision-language-action models, robot learning for manipulation and locomotion, embodied AI, and robot perception; contributes to policy selection and evaluation methods in humanoid and embodied robotics.

# World Models Dream of Success: Diagnosing and Repairing Failure Insensitivity in Robot World Models

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.09134.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Identified failure insensitivity in robot world models across multiple architectures and checkpoints
- Introduced CureWM, a method to construct and verify counterfactual failure data from successful demonstrations
- Fine-tuned released models using execution-verified failures and surviving successes without changing architecture or training objectives
- Demonstrated significant reduction in optimistic failure predictions on held-out counterfactuals and physical robot evaluations
- Showed counterfactual failures yield better success-failure discrimination than freshly collected on-policy failures
- Provided open-source code for reproducibility

### Method
CureWM constructs alternative actions from successful demonstrations along a severity grid, verifies outcomes via simulation or hardware execution, and fine-tunes existing robot world models on these verified failures and surviving successes alongside nominal data, enabling post-hoc repair without altering model architecture or objectives.

### Result
Fine-tuning with CureWM reduced failure optimism from 80% to 30-43% on 484 held-out failure counterfactuals and decreased success-like failure predictions from 90% to 33% on a physical robot arm; counterfactual failures improved success-failure value gap substantially compared to on-policy failures.

### Relevance
MEDIUM INTEREST: The work addresses robot world models' sensitivity to failure, improving predictive accuracy and robustness, which indirectly supports better goal reasoning and behaviour adaptation in embodied agents. However, it does not directly demonstrate agents forming or revising goals from experience or long-term memory effects on social interactions, placing it in medium relevance for the target profile.

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.20597.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces CoPE, a method that co-evolves acting and forecasting in language agents via multi-step action targets.
- Leverages successful on-policy trajectories to train a shared policy backbone to predict future action sequences, enabling temporal ensemble learning.
- Achieves stronger aggregate performance than GRPO and RL baselines across five benchmarks including realistic applications.
- Improves sample efficiency up to 1.9x and 2.0x compared to ECHO and GRPO on ScienceWorld.

### Method
CoPE trains language agents by supervising multi-step action sequences predicted from preceding histories on successful trajectories, enabling co-evolution of acting and forecasting within a shared policy backbone without inference overhead.

### Result
CoPE outperforms existing RL baselines with predictive auxiliary targets across multiple benchmarks, delivering higher sample efficiency and improved overall performance on realistic agent tasks.

### Relevance
High relevance to LLM-based autonomous agents and agentic frameworks, particularly in improving agent training efficiency and performance without added inference cost; aligns with interests in agent memory, reasoning, and evaluation benchmarks.

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced Semantically UNified (SUN) Programs integrating task semantics into control and learning

- Aligned geometric and contact relations across MPC costs, RL rewards, and diagnostics to preserve task semantics

### Method
Kuafu system automatically synthesizes typed SUN Programs from language and scene semantics, compiles them into aligned MPC costs, satisfaction predicates, RL rewards, and diagnostics, and screens feasibility via MPC to train stage-conditioned policies preserving task semantics.

Kuafu achieved 82.03% macro-success across nine tasks, outperforming sparse-reward (35.67%) and Stage-BC (24.75%) baselines; generated 10.57x more successful trajectory time per hour than human teleoperation at scale; trained DP3 policies with 46.0% simulation success and 34.7% success on physical Franka and Kinova robots without demonstrations or manual rewards.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to embodied AI, robot learning for manipulation, vision-language-action models, sim-to-real transfer, and dexterous manipulation, addressing key challenges in unifying symbolic planning and data-driven execution for physical robots.

# Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.22368.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces Value as Memory (VaM), using recent value predictions as task-progress memory to guide robot actions.
- Combines offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for online real-world policy improvement.
- Enables a transition from offline RL warmup to autonomous online learning under sparse rewards.

### Method
Value caching conditions a general robot policy on recent value predictions; online RL updates it using demonstrations, interventions, and live rollouts, with concurrent data collection and training.

### Result
Across long-horizon deformable-object and contact-rich manipulation tasks, value caching improves mean success rate by 29.4%, and online learning improves it by 32.8% over matched offline training. The online schedule runs 8× as many policy iterations at the same gradient-step budget and records over 2× lower time per gradient step.

### Relevance
High relevance to robot learning and reinforcement learning for manipulation, embodied AI, and physical-world learning; demonstrates sample-efficient real-world adaptation for general robot policies.

# DLAM: Distributional Latent Actions with Temporal Constraints

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/07/2607.27138.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces DLAM, a distributional latent-action model with diagonal Gaussian transitions.
- Incorporates temporal constraints via normalized composition and reversal over equal-gap triplets.
- Uses variance composition with shared-correlation coefficients to model dependence between adjacent transitions.
- Freezes encoder and trains flow-matching policy to jointly generate latent transitions and robot actions.
- Demonstrates improved temporal consistency and reconstruction over existing latent-action baselines.
- Shows enhanced policy performance on MetaWorld MT50, LIBERO, and real-world manipulation tasks.

### Method
DLAM models latent action transitions as diagonal Gaussians conditioned on reference frames, applying normalized composition and reversal constraints to mean and variance. Variance composition accounts for correlation between adjacent transitions. A flow-matching policy is trained on frozen encoder outputs to generate latent transitions and robot actions jointly.

### Result
DLAM achieves more temporally consistent latent dynamics and stronger direct and cumulative reconstruction on held-out videos compared to baselines. It improves downstream policy performance on multiple robotic manipulation benchmarks and real-world tasks. Ablations confirm the importance of normalized mean constraints and complementary benefits of learned variance and correlation-aware composition.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to vision-language-action models, robot learning for manipulation, embodied AI, sim-to-real transfer, and physical AI. Advances latent action modeling and policy learning applicable to humanoid robotics, robot perception, and dexterous manipulation.
note.title: DLAM: Distributional Latent Actions with Temporal Constraints

# LeFlow: Generative Latent Flow Planning for World Models

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/08/2608.24855.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces LeFlow, a reusable latent trajectory prior for planning in latent world models
- Recasts planning as conditional latent trajectory generation in latent dynamics space
- Uses a rectified-flow model to generate future latent paths between current and goal states
- Employs an inverse dynamics decoder to convert latent transitions into action sequences
- Demonstrates significant speedup and success-rate improvement over iterative action-space optimization
- Validates approach on four major goal-conditioned pixel-control benchmarks

### Method
LeFlow learns a latent trajectory prior operating in the latent dynamics space of a frozen world model, using a rectified-flow model for conditional latent trajectory generation and an inverse dynamics decoder to produce action chunks, verified by autoregressive rollout for planning.

### Result
LeFlow achieves consistent success-rate gains with an order-of-magnitude reduction in planning time compared to iterative action-space optimization across multiple benchmarks.

### Relevance
High interest for embodied AI, robot learning for manipulation and locomotion, vision-language-action models, robot navigation, and sim-to-real transfer due to its novel approach to amortized planning in latent world models enabling efficient and reusable planning priors.

# Learning Action Priors for Cross-embodiment Robot Manipulation

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/06/2606.26095.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced a two-stage training framework to pretrain action modules with motion priors before Vision-Language-Action (VLA) alignment.
- Developed a flow-matching-based encoder-decoder action module that learns temporal motion structure from unconditioned action trajectories without visual or language input.
- Transferred learned motion priors to VLA training via decoder reuse and latent distillation, enabling better cross-modal alignment and end-to-end policy refinement.
- Utilized the trained encoder as a compact history compressor for efficient history-aware modeling.
- Validated approach across 13 diverse cross-embodiment tasks on simulated and real-world platforms, demonstrating faster convergence and higher success rates.
- Showed that scaling up action data in pretraining improves generalizability and downstream VLA performance.

### Method
A two-stage training approach where Stage 1 pretrains an action module using flow-matching on unconditioned action trajectories to learn temporal motion priors, and Stage 2 transfers these priors to VLA training through decoder reuse and latent distillation for improved cross-modal alignment and policy refinement.

### Result
The proposed method achieves faster convergence, higher success rates, and stronger performance on data-scarce real-world cross-embodiment tasks compared to VLA training without action priors; scaling action data further enhances generalizability and downstream performance.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to humanoid robotics, embodied AI, robot learning for manipulation, vision-language-action models, sim-to-real transfer, and foundation models applied to robotics, aligning well with the target profile's high-interest areas.

# Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/08/2608.24885.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced WorldEcho benchmark to evaluate action following in world models beyond expert demonstrations
- Diagnosed limitations of current world models in following diverse off-expert actions
- Proposed WorldSync method to improve action-conditioned generation via distributional coverage, representational grounding, and intervention-effect alignment
- Demonstrated improved action following and visual validity in simulated and real-robot tasks
- Enabled more reliable simulators for iterative policy improvement leading to higher success rates

### Method
WorldSync enhances action-conditioned world models by broadening training action distributions, grounding video representations in robot dynamics through an Action-Forcing Expert, and aligning predicted changes with ground-truth futures under action interventions.

### Result
WorldSync improved WorldEcho benchmark metrics and outperformed prior models on RoboTwin and real-robot tasks, enabling policies to achieve higher success rates through more faithful action-conditioned generation.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to robot learning from demonstration and reinforcement learning for manipulation and locomotion, embodied AI, robot perception, sim-to-real transfer, and foundation models applied to robotics, addressing key challenges in action-conditioned world modeling for policy learning.

# T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.22364.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces a learnable environment latent that captures hidden physical properties and environmental rules without explicit labels.
- Separates training into world-model learning across environments and latent optimization through prediction.
- Adapts to unseen environments by optimizing a newly initialized latent from test-time interactions.
- Shows emergent latents represent individual and combined environmental factors across visual scenes.

### Method
T2-Z freezes the world model while optimizing an environment-conditioning latent from one or more interaction trajectories at test time; training alternates between world-model and latent optimization.

### Result
Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, object prediction error fell from 15.20 to 7.00 and action success rose from 33.73% to 72.96%. Ablations show adaptation can use a single test-time trajectory.

### Relevance
High relevance to embodied AI, robot learning, physical world understanding, and sim-to-real adaptation: the method helps robotic world models infer hidden environmental conditions and improve action outcomes.

# InfiniHand: Streaming World-Space Hand Motion Estimation from Egocentric Video

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/09/2609.35743.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces InfiniHand, an end-to-end streaming framework for world-space hand motion estimation from egocentric video
- Jointly estimates MANO hand parameters, camera trajectories, and hand locations without relying on separate SLAM or pose estimation modules
- Integrates persistent spatiotemporal memory with hand-centered visual features to couple camera motion and hand geometry
- Trains on a large-scale pretraining corpus (~5,000 hours) from multiple egocentric datasets
- Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with 21.4% reduction in ARCTIC PA-p error compared to ViDiHand
- Operates in real-time at 11.19 FPS with over twice the throughput of previous methods

### Method
End-to-end streaming feed-forward neural architecture combining spatiotemporal memory and hand-centered visual features to jointly estimate hand pose and camera motion from uncalibrated egocentric video, trained progressively with large-scale egocentric data.

### Result
Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on in-domain benchmarks with significant error reduction and mitigated world-space drift; generalizes robustly to in-the-wild videos; runs at real-time speeds (11.19 FPS) with high throughput.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to humanoid robotics, embodied AI, robot perception, and dexterous manipulation by enabling accurate real-time hand motion estimation and camera tracking from egocentric video, facilitating improved physical world understanding and robot learning from demonstration.

# Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/08/2608.18077.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced Hydra-0, a generalist world model conditioned on action flow representing robot actions as pixel motion
- Enabled generalist world modeling and control across embodiments, tasks, environments, and video-generation backbones
- Achieved significant reduction in robot-motion and object-motion errors compared to action-conditioned baseline
- Demonstrated zero-shot composition and data-efficient adaptation capabilities
- Uncovered an emergent inverse model predicting robot motion from desired object flow without task-specific expert demonstrations
- Validated performance on RoboLab benchmark with high correlation between replayed and reference success rates

### Method
Hydra-0 uses a shared visual interface representing robot actions as pixel motion (action flow) to learn action consequences across diverse settings, employing a world action model and trained action head to map latent features to executable actions without expert demonstrations.

### Result
Hydra-0 achieved 90.4% lower robot-motion error and 60.2% lower object-motion error than baseline, supported zero-shot composition and data-efficient adaptation, and reached a Pearson correlation of r=0.96 on RoboLab benchmark between replayed and reference success rates.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to humanoid robotics, whole-body control, embodied AI, robot learning from demonstration, vision-language-action models, robot perception, sim-to-real transfer, foundation models in robotics, and dexterous manipulation, aligning with high-interest areas in the target profile.

# Zero-WAM: In-Context World-Action Modeling from Human Videos for Open-Ended Task Generalization

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/08/2608.26103.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced Zero-WAM, a causal video-action model for zero-shot cross-task generalization in robotic manipulation.
- Developed an automatic pipeline to generate HumanGen, a large dataset of 74.2K human-robot in-context learning pairs across 8.6K tasks.
- Proposed an in-context future chunk prediction (IFP) training objective to enhance task understanding from human video prompts.
- Demonstrated significant performance improvement over baselines with 47.0% success rate on seven unseen RoboTwin 2.0 tasks.
- Validated real-world generalization to complex multi-object, long-horizon, and fine-grained manipulation tasks guided by human videos.

### Method
Zero-WAM leverages in-context learning by using human videos as task specifications to guide robotic manipulation without parameter updates, trained on HumanGen dataset with an IFP objective to suppress shortcuts and enforce task comprehension.

### Result
Achieved a 47.0% average success rate on unseen tasks in simulation, outperforming the strongest baseline by 29.5 percentage points, and demonstrated effective real-world generalization to complex manipulation scenarios.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to humanoid robotics, robot learning from demonstration, vision-language-action models, sim-to-real transfer, and dexterous manipulation, aligning with the target profile's high interest areas in embodied AI and physical world understanding.

- Introduced FlowWAM, a dual-stream diffusion framework using optical flow as a unified action representation for world action models.

# Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.22368.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces Value as Memory (VaM), using recent value predictions as task-progress memory to guide robot actions.
- Combines offline demonstrations, off-policy interventions, and on-policy rollouts for online real-world policy improvement.
- Enables a transition from offline RL warmup to autonomous online learning under sparse rewards.

### Method
Value caching conditions a general robot policy on recent value predictions; online RL updates it using demonstrations, interventions, and live rollouts, with concurrent data collection and training.

### Result
Across long-horizon deformable-object and contact-rich manipulation tasks, value caching improves mean success rate by 29.4%, and online learning improves it by 32.8% over matched offline training. The online schedule runs 8× as many policy iterations at the same gradient-step budget and records over 2× lower time per gradient step.

### Relevance
High relevance to robot learning and reinforcement learning for manipulation, embodied AI, and physical-world learning; demonstrates sample-efficient real-world adaptation for general robot policies.
note.title: Value as Memory: Online Value-Guided Post-training for General Robot Policies

# World Models Dream of Success: Diagnosing and Repairing Failure Insensitivity in Robot World Models

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.09134.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Identified failure insensitivity in robot world models across multiple architectures and checkpoints
- Introduced CureWM, a method to construct and verify counterfactual failure data from successful demonstrations
- Fine-tuned released models using execution-verified failures and surviving successes without changing architecture or training objectives
- Demonstrated significant reduction in optimistic failure predictions on held-out counterfactuals and physical robot evaluations
- Showed counterfactual failures yield better success-failure discrimination than freshly collected on-policy failures
- Provided open-source code for reproducibility

### Method
CureWM constructs alternative actions from successful demonstrations along a severity grid, verifies outcomes via simulation or hardware execution, and fine-tunes existing robot world models on these verified failures and surviving successes alongside nominal data, enabling post-hoc repair without altering model architecture or objectives.

### Result
Fine-tuning with CureWM reduced failure optimism from 80% to 30-43% on 484 held-out failure counterfactuals and decreased success-like failure predictions from 90% to 33% on a physical robot arm; counterfactual failures improved success-failure value gap substantially compared to on-policy failures.

### Relevance
MEDIUM INTEREST: The work addresses robot world models' sensitivity to failure, improving predictive accuracy and robustness, which indirectly supports better goal reasoning and behaviour adaptation in embodied agents. However, it does not directly demonstrate agents forming or revising goals from experience or long-term memory effects on social interactions, placing it in medium relevance for the target profile.

# Lift3D-VLA: Lifting VLA Models to 3D Geometry and Dynamics-Aware Manipulation

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/07/2607.06564.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced Lift3D-VLA, a unified Vision-Language-Action framework with explicit 3D point cloud reasoning
- Proposed enhanced 2D model-lifting strategy to align 3D points with pretrained 2D positional embeddings
- Developed Geometry-Centric Masked Autoencoding (GC-MAE) for self-supervised learning of 3D structure and dynamics
- Designed layer-wise temporal action modeling leveraging multiple LLM layers for temporally consistent action prediction
- Achieved significant performance improvements on 22 simulated and 8 real-world manipulation tasks compared to prior VLA methods

### Method
Lift3D-VLA integrates explicit 3D point cloud encoding within the vision encoder using an enhanced 2D model-lifting strategy, employs Geometry-Centric Masked Autoencoding for dual-objective self-supervised learning of current and future 3D geometry, and utilizes layer-wise temporal action modeling in the LLM to predict temporally coherent action sequences.

### Result
Lift3D-VLA outperforms prior state-of-the-art VLA methods by 10.8% and 11.1% mean success rates on MetaWorld and RLBench benchmarks respectively, and exceeds the strongest real-world baseline by 4 percentage points, demonstrating stronger generalization to out-of-distribution perturbations.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to embodied AI, robot learning for manipulation, vision-language-action models, physical world understanding, and sim-to-real transfer; aligns with high interest areas including dexterous manipulation and foundation models applied to robotics.

# CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.22362.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces CoDA, a framework for co-evolving simulation environment generation and robot action policies.
- Uses shared memory of validated failure diagnoses and learning progress to create targeted environment and training programs.
- Presents Text2potential, which turns diagnoses into staged potentials for dense action-chunk value learning while preserving the optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions.

### Method
A vision-language critic diagnoses policy failures; validated diagnoses are stored and compiled into programs that recreate challenging environments and provide targeted training. Learning progress guides iterative generation and refinement.

### Result
Across four manipulation task families, out-of-distribution success rises from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, beating the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points at the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.

### Relevance
High relevance to robot learning for manipulation, embodied AI, and simulation-based policy training. The work addresses targeted failure recovery and robustness to distribution shifts, though it does not specifically focus on humanoid or whole-body control.

IMGEP architecture combining self-generated goals, intrinsic reward-based goal selection, incremental goal-parameterized policy search, batch learning exploitation, and systematic information reuse; implemented with AMB variant featuring population-based policies and spatio-temporal modularity.

Successfully enabled a humanoid robot to autonomously explore and learn multiple complex skills across hundreds of continuous goal dimensions, generating an automatic learning curriculum without external goal specification.

### Relevance

# Benchmarking LLM Agents on Meta-Analysis Articles from Nature Portfolio

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/06/2606.17041.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced MetaSyn dataset with 442 expert-curated meta-analyses from Nature Portfolio
- Provided a retrieval corpus of 140k PubMed articles with verified positive studies and hard negatives
- Established complete search strategies and date bounds for meta-analysis evaluation
- Benchmarked twelve pipeline configurations including nine RAG variants and a protocol-driven agent
- Identified a critical screening bottleneck limiting recovery of ground-truth literature to 52.7% despite high retrieval recall
- Demonstrated that current LLMs struggle to distinguish eligible studies from PI/ECO-ineligible distractors in similar topical pools

### Method
Developed MetaSyn dataset pairing research questions with PI/ECO criteria and retrieval corpus; evaluated multiple pipeline configurations including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) variants and protocol-driven agents on the meta-analysis retrieval-screening-synthesis pipeline.

### Result
Found a retrieval ceiling of 90.9% recall at K=200 but screening bottleneck limits literature recovery to 52.7%; stage-attributed metrics reveal system strengths and weaknesses, showing that single end-to-end scores are insufficient.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to knowledge graph construction, RAG architectures and evaluation, hybrid retrieval methods, memory systems for LLMs, provenance tracking, semantic search, and structured extraction; addresses challenges in retrieval and screening critical for knowledge representation and retrieval systems.

# Tables Decoded: DELTA for Structure, TARQA for Understanding

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/09/2609.17458.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Proposed DELTA system separating physical and logical structure recognition plus OCR for accurate table layout and content extraction
- Introduced Optimised Table Structure Language (OTSL) for compact unified table representation
- Developed TARQA, an LLM fine-tuned on OTSL sequences for improved table visual question answering
- Demonstrated DELTA's state-of-the-art performance on multiple table structure recognition benchmarks including multilingual robustness
- Achieved significant gains in TabVQA tasks (WTQ and FinTabNetQA) using TARQA
- Released code, models, and benchmarks publicly to support reproducibility and further research

### Method
DELTA extracts table layout and content by separating physical structure recognition, logical structure recognition, and OCR, outputting tables in OTSL format; TARQA fine-tunes a large language model on OTSL sequences for table visual question answering.

### Result
DELTA achieves comparable or superior TEDS-Structure scores on FinTabNet, PubTabNet, and PubTables-1M; robust performance on Hindi TORQUE benchmark; TARQA improves TabVQA accuracy by over 9 percentage points on WTQ and FinTabNetQA; ranks second on TORQUE among VLMs and DELTA+LLM variants.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to document understanding and structured extraction, semantic search, knowledge graph construction, and memory systems for LLMs; introduces scalable structured textual representations aligning with LLMs, facilitating multilingual and robust knowledge extraction; supports retrieval-augmented generation architectures and knowledge base population through improved table understanding.

# Attention over noisy examples: generalization and memorization in the exponential Hopfield network

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.22191.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Analyzes learning noisy archetypes in the exponential Hopfield network, whose zero-temperature update is softmax attention over examples.
- Derives a closed-form generalization overlap governed by an effective attention entropy.
- Shows that, in a temperature window widening as √N, interference becomes exponentially small and learnable archetype capacity can grow as exp(c√N).
- Identifies memorization as a random-energy-model freezing transition and links it to softmax concentration on the nearest training example.
- Validates the memorization diagnostic on MNIST and finds that fashion-MNIST sub-clusters can make local sub-prototype readout beneficial.

### Method
Signal-to-noise analysis of exponential Hopfield retrieval from multiple noisy examples per archetype; interprets example-level softmax weights using the random energy model and evaluates the resulting diagnostic on MNIST and fashion-MNIST.

### Result
Generalization overlap follows an error-function law with effective attention entropy. The exponential model suppresses archetype interference over a broad temperature regime, while its failure mode is example memorization rather than a spin-glass phase. On fashion-MNIST, accuracy can peak beyond the memorization threshold by reading out local sub-prototypes.

### Relevance

# Toy Models of Initialisation Effects on RL Dynamics

## Archive
path: rss/2026/07/lesswrong-high-karma-2026-07-14-36906629f3.html

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces toy mathematical models illustrating rich-get-richer dynamics in reinforcement learning (RL)
- Demonstrates how initialisation affects RL learning trajectories and final policies
- Models underspecified behaviours where reward functions do not constrain certain aspects of model behaviour
- Extends analysis to cognition-level underspecification, showing different cognitive patterns can yield identical in-distribution behaviour but diverge out-of-distribution
- Provides proofs and simulations supporting the dynamics of policy gradient learning under softmax parameterisation
- Proposes concrete research directions to empirically test and extend these toy models in real-world neural network training

### Method
Develops and analyses simple mathematical and simulation-based toy models of RL learning dynamics using softmax parameterised policies, including deterministic full-gradient and finite-sample stochastic updates (RLOO). Extends models to latent cognitive pattern mixtures to study cognition-level underspecification. Uses visualisations on probability simplexes and formal proofs to illustrate dynamics.

### Result
Shows that RL learning exhibits rich-get-richer dynamics where initial policy probabilities strongly influence final learned behaviours, including convergence to suboptimal or hacking solutions. Demonstrates that reward underspecification leads to persistence of initial behavioural traits. Reveals that different cognitive motivations can produce indistinguishable in-distribution behaviour but diverge out-of-distribution, highlighting challenges for alignment. Provides formal proofs of these dynamics and suggests empirical research directions.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to AI alignment theory, fundamental AI learning theory, interpretability and mechanistic understanding of neural networks, and emergent capabilities in large models. Offers theoretical insights into how initialisation and reward underspecification impact RL dynamics and cognition, informing AGI frameworks and meta-learning theory. Less relevant to applied agent systems or engineering-focused ML without theoretical novelty.

# Foundation Models for Oversight

## Archive
path: rss/2026/07/lesswrong-high-karma-2026-07-29-b3cd4550e8.html

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces Pythonic world models to formalize AI oversight tasks as Bayesian inference problems
- Proposes a universal training objective for oversight via autoregressive prediction of Pythonic world model outputs
- Develops a scalable data generation pipeline leveraging arXiv papers to create diverse oversight experiments
- Presents RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verified Rewards) to efficiently target rare, narrow oversight behaviors
- Outlines a staged de-risking plan for scaling oversight models from individual tasks to zero-shot generalization
- Demonstrates post-training methods to align oversight models with natural language queries while preserving capabilities

### Method
The approach casts AI oversight as a world modeling problem using Pythonic world models that express interventions and measurements on a subject model via Python code. Oversight questions are formalized as Bayesian inference over these models, which is reduced to an autoregressive prediction task suitable for transformer training. Diverse training data is generated by converting ML experiments from arXiv papers into executable Python programs and sampling inputs. RLVR is introduced to train models to propose distributions over variables to hit rare oversight targets efficiently. A staged scale-up and de-risking plan is proposed, culminating in post-training for natural language interaction and human-aligned explanations.

### Result
A detailed framework and roadmap for building foundation models specialized in AI oversight, capable of formalizing complex oversight questions, producing trustworthy empirical data, and generalizing across diverse tasks. The method promises scalable training on large, diverse datasets with theoretical grounding in Bayesian inference and probabilistic programming, enabling improved interpretability, alignment, and evaluation of AI systems.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to fundamental AI theory, interpretability, mechanistic understanding of neural networks, AI alignment theory, causal reasoning, meta-learning, and emergent capabilities in large models. The work introduces novel paradigms combining symbolic reasoning with neural architectures and provides theoretical and practical advances in AI oversight, aligning closely with the target profile's high-interest areas.

SWE-Stream progressively constructs and validates executable training tasks from development histories by reusing artifacts and applying targeted completion, coordinated by an elastic scheduler that adapts execution budgets asynchronously under shared resource constraints.

Constructed a large dataset of validated tasks and trajectories enabling fine-tuning of a 30B parameter model that achieved 69.0%, 49.3%, and 45.42% resolve rates on SWE-bench Verified, Multilingual, and Pro benchmarks respectively, outperforming existing data sources and improving task throughput by 1.45x over batch methods.

- Collected 2,269 real-world multi-round code review tasks across five programming languages
- Annotated tasks with fine-grained defect metadata and dynamic state labels capturing defect evolution
- Conducted extensive experiments evaluating mainstream LLMs on defect detection and lifecycle tracking
- Identified LLM limitations including performance degradation over multiple review rounds and sensitivity to defect type and severity
- Performed in-depth error analysis revealing key failure mechanisms like temporal misalignment and limited long-range memory

### Method
Developed MCR-Bench dataset with multi-round code review tasks annotated for defect states and metadata; evaluated mainstream large language models on this benchmark to assess their capabilities in defect detection and lifecycle tracking through iterative review rounds.

### Result
Mainstream LLMs show limited overall performance in multi-round code review tasks, with accuracy decreasing as interaction rounds increase; performance varies significantly by defect type and severity, with complex or low-salience defects often missed; error analysis highlights critical weaknesses such as cross-round temporal misalignment and insufficient long-range memory.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to AI-assisted code review and refactoring, AI coding assistants' capabilities, prompt engineering for code generation, and evaluation of LLMs on realistic coding tasks; provides valuable insights for improving AI tools in multi-round interactive software engineering workflows.

# EngramBench: A Capability-Grounded Benchmark for Skill-Evolution Harnesses

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/09/2609.39284.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces EngramBench, a capability-grounded benchmark for evaluating skill evolution in AI coding agents
- Defines strict axiom of capability overlap without solution overlap to avoid rote solution leakage
- Provides 30 diverse learning tasks and 13 unseen transfer tasks simulating multi-hour development cycles
- Demonstrates that static skill banks reduce redundant context and coding time by over 55% but do not replace base model reasoning
- Shifts evaluation paradigm from pattern matching to verifiable deep cross-domain capability transfer
- Validates findings with extensive multi-hour execution trajectories and human-expert review

### Method
Developed EngramBench benchmark with interactive, multi-hour coding tasks driven by LLM-simulated users; evaluated 48 execution trajectories with human expert validation to measure genuine capability abstraction versus rote copying.

### Result
Found that genuine capability abstraction significantly reduces redundant context and coding time by over 55%, serving as an execution compass, but exact code implementation remains limited by base model reasoning capabilities.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to AI coding assistants, agentic coding workflows, AI-assisted code review, debugging with LLMs, prompt engineering for code generation, autonomous software engineering agents, and developer experience with AI tools; represents a step-change in evaluating AI-assisted software development capabilities.

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces WEAVE, a framework that converts verified pull-request histories into executable, dependency-structured coding tasks.

### Result
WEAVE produces coherent executable tasks and measures partial progress more faithfully than flat scoring; its tasks and rewards provide effective supervision for training code agents.

### Relevance
High: directly advances benchmarks, evaluation, and training for autonomous coding agents on realistic, long-horizon software engineering tasks.

# SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/08/2608.23564.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduced SWE Refactor Bench, a benchmark with 20 whole-repository migrations covering 4 types of technical debt
- Developed a three-stage evaluation protocol measuring migration completeness and behavioral correctness
- Demonstrated that current coding agents rarely achieve perfect whole-repository migrations (5.4% success rate)
- Identified distinct challenges between migration completeness and behavioral correctness
- Showed agent performance varies significantly across migration categories
- Positioned SWE Refactor Bench as a rigorous testbed for advancing AI coding agents in complex refactoring tasks

### Method
Designed SWE Refactor Bench with 20 real-world repository migrations and a three-stage evaluation: Migration Audit to verify migration occurrence, Behavioral Tests with fixed test suites, and Agentic Verification using 6 independent coding agents to generate targeted tests for hidden behavioral differences. Evaluated 8 state-of-the-art models across 520 runs.

### Result
Only 28 of 520 runs (5.4%) passed all evaluation stages; 13 of 20 tasks had no accepted solution; best model scored 47.0/100. Migration completeness and behavioral correctness are distinct; many runs either skip migration or break behavior. Agent capability varies by migration type, scoring highest on build toolchain rewrites and lowest on language rewrites.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to AI coding assistants, agentic coding workflows, AI-assisted code review and refactoring, test generation with AI, debugging with LLMs, prompt engineering for code tasks, and autonomous software engineering agents. Provides critical insights and a benchmark for improving AI tools in whole-repository migrations and complex refactoring.

# Stateful Testing for Deep Learning Compilers

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.22003.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Identifies compiler state retained across invocations as a source of bugs missed by isolated tests.
- Models tests as a program plus an invocation sequence, then mutates sequences to explore stateful behavior.
- Uses a three-way differential oracle: uncompiled execution, compiled execution with reset state, and compiled execution with retained state.
- Replays suspected failures under controlled state conditions and shortens invocation sequences while preserving the bug.

### Method
Rondo combines invocation-sequence mutation with an MCMC sampler guided by compilation behavior, then applies differential testing, controlled replay, and sequence reduction.

### Result
Across four frameworks and 24 model architectures, Rondo detected 117 bugs, including 35 stateful bugs. Developers confirmed 35 reports and fixed 18 bugs. It achieved 99.26% alarm precision and shortened 44 sequences by 83.34% on average.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to testing strategy, debugging, and reliability: it demonstrates practical ways to expose hidden state-dependent failures, improve test coverage, and produce minimal, reproducible bug cases. The techniques transfer to stateful services and APIs beyond deep learning compilers.

### Method
Within-subjects user study with 34 participants reviewing real-world code changes using three LLM-based code review conditions varying in XAI support (detailed explanation, review feedback only, no explanation). Measured trust, agreement, reasoning, and time.

# From Bug Reports to Browser-Executable Procedures: An LLM-Driven Agent for Web GUI Bug Reproduction

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/08/2608.03598.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces ReBug, an LLM-driven agent that reconstructs and executes browser-level bug reproduction procedures from natural-language web GUI bug reports
- Separates bug reproduction into preparation (context reconstruction and plan generation) and execution (tool-mediated browser interactions and state validation) stages
- Maintains structured summaries of page state and action history to validate reproduction outcomes against report expectations
- Evaluates ReBug on 667 real-world bug reports from open-source web applications, demonstrating superior reproduction success rates compared to baselines
- Shows that explicit context reconstruction and state-aware execution effectively support automated web GUI bug reproduction
- Demonstrates that successful reproduction procedures can expose original buggy behaviors on restored versions

### Method
ReBug uses a context-aware LLM agent to reconstruct missing prerequisites from bug reports and artifacts, generates a high-level reproduction plan, then drives a real browser with tool-mediated interactions while maintaining structured state summaries and validating final states against expected outcomes derived from the reports.

### Result
ReBug achieved an average reproduction success rate (RSR) of 49.96%, mean task completion rate of 74.96%, and mean action execution success rate of 86.54% on 667 real-world web GUI bug reports, outperforming baseline methods and effectively reproducing bugs by driving a real browser.

### Relevance
High relevance to AI-assisted debugging, autonomous software engineering agents, and AI-driven coding workflows; demonstrates practical application of LLMs in reproducing and validating web GUI bugs, contributing to AI coding assistants and debugging with LLM assistance.

# Can LLMs Fix It Without Code? Toward Automated Verification of No-Code Bug Fixes

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.11963.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Proposed an automated execution-based pipeline to evaluate LLM-generated no-code bug fixes in real browser environments
- Evaluated 322 no-code fixes across multiple bug categories using three different executor agents
- Demonstrated that executor choice significantly impacts fix resolution rates and verification outcomes
- Showed that fewer than half of LLM-generated no-code fixes reliably resolve bugs without verification
- Compared executor verdicts to human consensus, highlighting variability and need for verification
- Provided insights into the limitations and verification needs of AI-generated no-code fixes before user deployment

### Method
Developed a pipeline where executor agents apply LLM-generated no-code fixes by following natural language instructions in a browser environment; issue-specific checkers then assess if the bug persists; repeated with three different executor agents to compare effectiveness.

### Result
Only 17.6% of candidate issues passed setup and sanity checks; fix resolution rates varied from 14.6% to 49.7% depending on executor, with the best configuration resolving up to 74.1%; executor choice shifted resolution rates by an average of 38.8%; executor-human consensus ranged from 66.1% to 88.1%; fewer than half of fixes reliably resolved bugs without verification.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to AI coding assistants, agentic coding workflows, debugging with LLM assistance, and AI-assisted software engineering; provides critical evaluation of LLM capabilities in no-code bug fixing and highlights the importance of execution-based verification for reliable AI-assisted development.

# When Commodore tried to turn the C64 into a console, it backfired spectacularly

## Archive
path: inbox/2026/06/a0d948b113.html

## Summary
### Contributions
- Commodore 64 Games System (C64GS) was a keyboardless console version of the Commodore 64 released in 1990.
- C64GS reused C64 hardware but removed keyboard and ports, focusing on cartridge-based gaming.
- The lack of keyboard limited game compatibility, as many C64 games required keyboard input.
- C64GS targeted families wanting simple gaming but failed due to limited software library and competition from Nintendo and Sega.
- Commercially unsuccessful, it highlighted Commodore's strategic challenges and inability to adapt the C64 to console market.
- C64GS is of historical interest to Commodore 64 enthusiasts and retro computing collectors.

### Method
Extracted key factual points from detailed article about C64GS focusing on hardware, software, market impact, and relevance to Commodore 64 community.

### Result
The C64GS was a Commodore attempt to convert the popular Commodore 64 into a cartridge-based console by removing the keyboard and ports. While hardware was largely reused, the removal of the keyboard severely limited game compatibility, as many titles required keyboard input. The system targeted families wanting simple console gaming but failed commercially due to limited adapted software, competition from established consoles, and internal competition with the full C64. The C64GS is now a collector's item and a case study in the challenges of repurposing a computer as a console.

### Relevance
HIGH INTEREST for Commodore 64 and Commodore 128 enthusiasts interested in hardware projects, software compatibility issues, and historical context of Commodore's console attempts.

# QuSema: Detecting Silent Bugs in Quantum Libraries via Quantum-knowledge-enhanced Agents

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.10258.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces QuSema, an autonomous testing agent for detecting silent bugs in quantum libraries
- Uses quantum semantics and documentation as source-level semantic oracles for bug detection
- Implements an agentic loop combining code inspection, reasoning, and test generation
- Demonstrates superior bug detection on benchmarks compared to Claude Code and Codex
- Discovers 40 previously unknown bugs in Qiskit and PennyLane, including 30 silent bugs

### Method
QuSema operates by repeatedly analyzing quantum library API documentation and source code to reason about intended quantum operation behavior, identifies semantic deviations, and validates them by generating executable tests through library APIs, guided by quantum-domain knowledge.

### Result
QuSema achieves higher mean bug relocation counts than existing AI coding assistants on a benchmark of 20 historical silent bugs and uncovers 40 previously unknown bugs confirmed by developers, demonstrating effective detection of non-crash defects in quantum libraries.

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces a bounded old-state modulation rule for Self-Modulating Quantum Fast-Weight Programmers (QFWPs) to prevent divergence in long sequences
- Identifies accumulated-memory modulation as the key mechanism driving Self-Modulating QFWP improvements
- Demonstrates that bounding the old-state gate enhances robustness and stability in quantum sequence modeling
- Evaluates variants of QFWP on quantum-dynamics forecasting and telecommunication activity prediction tasks
- Shows that old-state modulation consistently improves performance over standard QFWP
- Provides targeted stabilization strategy for quantum recurrent memory in sequence modeling

### Method
Proposes a sign-preserving tanh gate applied only to the recurrent memory branch in Self-Modulating QFWP, leaving additive and new-update modulations unchanged; evaluates this bounded gating approach against standard and ablated QFWP variants on quantum and real-world sequence prediction tasks.

### Result
Bounding the old-state modulation gate removes long-sequence divergence and improves aggregate robustness; old-state modulation is the most consistent source of performance gains; original unbounded Self-Modulating QFWP shows strongest gains at longer input windows, confirming accumulated-memory modulation as the key mechanism.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to novel neural network architectures with broad applicability, fundamental AI theory including learning and generalization, emergent capabilities in sequence modeling, and interpretability of neural mechanisms; introduces a new stabilization paradigm for quantum sequence models aligning with interests in theoretical AI and cognitive architectures.

# EvoDuet: Bilevel Co-Evolution of Web Searching and Task Solving for Scientific Discovery

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/09/2609.40340.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces EvoDuet, a bi-level co-evolutionary method combining web search and solution generation for scientific discovery with LLMs
- Develops a retrieval gate mechanism enabling LLMs to dynamically decide when to retrieve, reuse, or proceed without external documents
- Implements an inner loop optimizing search queries and document ranking based on predicted solution quality
- Demonstrates significant performance improvements on 21 optimization tasks with GPT-5.6-Luna and Gemini-3.8-Flash models
- Shows EvoDuet's compatibility and enhancement of various evolutionary search scaffolds like Top-K and EvoX
- Surpasses or matches previous best scores on multiple benchmark tasks, indicating strong empirical gains

### Method
EvoDuet employs a bi-level optimization framework where an outer loop generates candidate solutions using retrieved documents, and an inner loop refines search queries and ranks documents by predicted solution scores. A retrieval gate within the LLM assesses knowledge gaps to decide on document retrieval or reuse, enabling dynamic integration of external knowledge without changing model parameters.

### Result
EvoDuet improves normalized discovery gain from 74.1% to 78.0% with GPT-5.6-Luna and from 61.3% to 82.3% with Gemini-3.8-Flash across 21 tasks, surpassing previous best results on eight tasks and matching on three others. It also enhances other evolutionary search scaffolds, demonstrating broad applicability and effectiveness in scientific discovery tasks.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to LLM-based autonomous agents and agentic frameworks by advancing agentic retrieval-augmented generation and self-improvement mechanisms. The dynamic retrieval gate and co-evolution approach contribute to agent memory architectures, planning, tool use, and reflection. The method aligns with interests in agent evaluation and benchmarks, prompt engineering for agent control, and agent safety by improving autonomous scientific discovery capabilities.

# From Mirage to Grounding: Towards Reliable Multimodal Circuit-to-Verilog Code Generation

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/04/2604.27969.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Identification of the Mirage phenomenon where MLLMs bypass visual input by exploiting identifier semantics
- Creation of C2VEVAL benchmark with paired Normal/Anony evaluation protocol to quantify Mirage effect
- Development of VeriGround (4B), a model trained with identifier anonymization, refusal augmentation, and D-ORPO preference alignment
- Demonstration that VeriGround achieves strong functional accuracy with low false refusal rates and robust refusal on blank inputs
- Empirical evidence that VeriGround matches GPT-5.4 performance under Normal mode and outperforms all baselines under Anony mode
- Highlighting a covert defect in AI-assisted code generation that impacts trustworthiness and reliability of vision-to-code models

### Method
Constructed a paired Normal/Anony evaluation protocol anonymizing identifiers to expose reliance on header semantics; trained VeriGround with identifier anonymization, refusal augmentation, and Decision-Focused ORPO preference alignment to improve genuine visual grounding and refusal behavior.

### Result
VeriGround (4B) achieved Functional Pass@1 of 46.11% (Normal) and 42.51% (Anony) with only 1.20%/0.00% False Refusal Rate, maintained >92% refusal on blank images, matched GPT-5.4 performance in Normal mode, and significantly outperformed baselines in Anony mode, confirming effective visual grounding and improved reliability.

### Relevance
Addresses evaluation methods and practical AI engineering challenges in multimodal LLMs; introduces a novel defect affecting trustworthiness in vision-to-code generation; proposes training and evaluation strategies relevant for AI agents and multi-agent systems requiring reliable visual grounding and refusal mechanisms; provides benchmark and model implementation details useful for agentic system development.

# Aspire: Can Models Self-Evolve from Vague Goals?

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/08/2608.31111.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces ASPIRE, a benchmark for vague-goal-driven self-evolution in LLM-based agents
- Defines a framework where agents must interpret vague natural-language goals and autonomously select data, update methods, and evaluation strategies
- Supports both model-weight and agent-harness evolution within a unified interactive environment
- Evaluates agents on a hidden, expert-authored set of 520 tasks spanning six vague goals
- Demonstrates that current agents can complete training and harness-editing loops but show sparse and unstable weight-level improvements
- Identifies challenges such as training on mismatched data and overtrusting narrow self-evaluations leading to poor transfer and unstable gains

### Method
Develop ASPIRE benchmark providing only vague natural-language capability goals without explicit downstream tasks; agents autonomously operationalize goals by selecting training data, update methods, and evaluation signals; supports both model-weight and agent-harness evolution in an interactive environment; evaluates performance on hidden expert-authored tasks.

### Result
Current agents successfully perform training and harness-editing loops but achieve limited and unstable improvements at the model-weight level; strongest evolved agent harness underperforms engineered Qwen-Agent baseline; agents often train on mismatched data and rely on narrow self-evaluations, causing local gains to fail in hidden evaluations and earlier improvements to be erased by continued training.

### Relevance
HIGH INTEREST: Directly addresses LLM-based autonomous agents, agent self-improvement and reflection, agent evaluation and benchmarks, and agentic frameworks. The work advances understanding of agentic self-evolution from vague goals, relevant to multi-agent systems, agent memory, planning, and safety. MEDIUM INTEREST: Related to LLM fine-tuning for agent behavior and inference optimization. LOW INTEREST / EXCLUDE: Does not focus on general NLP, robotics, or standalone knowledge systems.

# FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/10/2610.22350.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces FDE-Gym, a benchmark of 95 end-to-end delivery tasks across 20 customer scenarios and 18 sectors.
- Simulates stakeholder interactions and modifiable, production-like customer systems to test agents on ambiguous requirements.
- Scores delivery by normalized improvement to customer success metrics, with penalties for interaction costs.
- Provides an online platform for human practice under the same evaluation criteria.

### Method
Evaluates 13 model configurations from seven providers on realistic and guided delivery tasks, measuring business uplift, task resolution, and stakeholder-interaction costs.

### Result
The best configuration scores 0.56 on realistic tasks and resolves 14 of 95 at the success threshold. Even when it obtains all key stakeholder facts on 23 tasks, it achieves business uplift of at least 0.8 on only 10, indicating that constraint discovery and effective execution remain major bottlenecks.

### Relevance
High relevance: a benchmark for autonomous agents operating tools and systems, eliciting requirements from stakeholders, and delivering outcomes under ambiguity. It exposes a substantial gap between solving specified tasks and real-world agent performance.

# SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments

## Archive
path: arxiv/2026/08/2608.19197.pdf

## Summary
### Contributions
- Introduces SPADE, a self-play RL framework where a single LLM acts as both Environment Designer and Reasoning Agent
- Designs adaptive, executable training environments with an OpenAI Gym-style interface
- Uses regret-based optimization to target environments at the edge of agent capabilities
- Incorporates environment memory and grounding on large pretraining corpus documents
- Demonstrates significant performance improvements on diverse benchmarks including math, science, code, and reasoning tasks
- Scales effectively with model size, enhancing tool-use and game-playing agent performance

### Method
SPADE employs a single large language model in dual roles: an Environment Designer that generates executable, long-horizon training environments with stateful interfaces, and a Reasoning Agent that learns to act within them. The Environment Designer adapts environments by optimizing a regret signal based on the Reasoning Agent's performance gap with and without privileged hints, enabling dynamic curriculum generation. The framework grounds environment design on sampled documents and maintains environment memory to improve adaptability.

### Result
SPADE achieves an average improvement of +5.3 points over the strongest fixed-environment baselines across eight held-out benchmarks in math, science, code, and reasoning. It further improves tool-use tasks by +5.7 on BFCL-v4 multi-turn and +13.9 on ACEBench-Agent, with performance gains increasing with model scale in game settings.

### Relevance
Highly relevant to LLM-based autonomous agents, agentic frameworks, multi-agent coordination, agent memory architectures, LLM planning and chain-of-thought reasoning, tool use, agent self-improvement, evaluation benchmarks, agentic retrieval-augmented generation, prompt engineering, and agent safety and alignment. Medium relevance to LLM fine-tuning for agents, RLHF in agent tasks, inference optimization for agents, and multi-modal agents without robotics focus. Low relevance to general NLP, pre-training without agent focus, computer vision without agent context, robotics, standalone knowledge graphs, general ML theory, and practical AI coding tools.
